title: Hunts man charged with seven counts of rape named for first time
content: A man from Huntingdonshire charged with rape and intentional strangulation is due in court. Toby Tiller, of Princes Street, Ramsey, is due to appear at Huntingdon Magistrates' Court for his first hearing on Tuesday (November 17). He faces seven counts of raping a woman aged 16 years of age or older and two counts of intentional strangulation. The 24-year-old is also accused of engaging in controlling or coercive behaviour in an intimate relationship. The alleged offences all said to have occurred in Cambridgeshire between August 2024 and May 2025. Have you got a story you want to share? title: Motorcyclist seriously injured after crash involving Audi in Hunts town
content: A motorcyclist has been seriously injured in a crash involving a car in a Huntingdonshire town. Police were called at 4.47pm on Saturday (November 14) to reports of a collision between an Audi Q3 and a motorbike in Great Whyte, Ramsey. Officers and paramedics attended and the motorcyclist was rushed to hospital with serious injuries, Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed. A spokesperson for the force said: "The Audi driver was unhurt and remained at the scene. "An investigation is ongoing, and anyone with information should contact us via the website or 101 quoting incident 360 of November 14." Have you got a story you want to share? title: Reform councillor complains to Parliament over MP’s response to 199-home plan
content: A Reform UK councillor has complained to Parliament about MP Sam Carling over a 199-home development between Ramsey and Bury. Cllr Karan Maheshwari, who represents Ramsey on Huntingdonshire District Council, has submitted a complaint to the Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards. It concerns North West Cambridgeshire MP Mr Carling’s response to Cllr Maheshwari’s request for him to intervene in planning application 25/01382/OUT, for 199 homes between Ramsey and Bury. A copy seen by this publication is dated November 2 and marked “DRAFT – NOT SUBMITTED”, but Cllr Maheshwari later confirmed he submitted it on November 3 and received confirmation on November 4. The dispute began after Huntingdonshire District Council’s development management committee said it was minded to reject the scheme. title: Here is some of Huntingdonshire's most unusual bridges and where to find them
content: From a medieval bridge with its own chapel to a 55-arch causeway, Huntingdonshire is packed with unusual crossings. The district’s rivers, floodplains and Fenland waterways have shaped travel for centuries, leaving medieval crossings and Fen drainage bridges behind. Here are some of Huntingdonshire’s most striking bridges and where to find them. St Ives Bridge One of the county’s most extraordinary bridges spans the River Great Ouse at St Ives. The town’s first bridge was built of wood in 1107, before work began on a stone replacement in the early 15th century. The stone crossing was completed in 1425, and a chapel was added the following year. It is one of only three bridges in England with a chapel. The bridge also still bears the scars of the English Civil War. Parliamentary troops destroyed part of it to hinder Royalist forces, so a temporary drawbridge was installed. When the damaged section was rebuilt in 1716, it was given rounded arches instead of matching the pointed medieval ones, leaving a visible difference today. title: Hunts man due in court accused of employee theft and fraud offences named
content: A Huntingdonshire man is due to appear in court accused of a string of fraud and theft offences. Matthew Stokes, 35, of Liberator Road, Ramsey, is accused of fraud by false representation and theft by an employee. His first hearing is due to take place on November 5 at Cambridge Magistrates' Court. He is alleged to have spent £935.83 on personal items using a company credit card while on leave between August 21 and September 2, knowing the transactions were unauthorised and intending to make financial gain. He is also accused of stealing an Apple iPhone worth £285, a Lenovo laptop worth £478 and several tools, including a drill set. The items belonged to water treatment supplier Prodose Ltd and were allegedly stolen between September 2 and October 14. Between November 13 and December 8, Mr Stokes is accused of stealing tools valued at £2,109.18 from Riverside Waste Machinery Ltd. A further fraud charge alleges that he used or permitted the use of company credit cards for unauthorised transactions totalling £412.41 between October 6 and December 8. All the offences are alleged to have taken place in Huntingdon.
summary: A Huntingdonshire man is due to appear in court accused of a string of fraud and theft offences. Matthew Stokes, 35, of Liberator Road, Ramsey, is accused of fraud by false representation and theft by an employee. His first hearing is due to take place on November 5 at Cambridge Magistrates' Court.

title: Plans submitted for four-caravan traveller site on land near Ramsey
content: Plans have been submitted to create a new residential traveller site for a family near Ramsey. The application, reference 26/01646/FUL, seeks permission to change the use of land on the south side of Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights, to accommodate four static caravans for residential use. The proposals also include parking for vehicles, space for two touring caravans and the construction of a brick and tile utility and day room for residents. Existing hardstanding at the site would be retained. Applicant Christopher Reilly is seeking permission for the development to provide a permanent home for his family, who are members of the Gypsy and Traveller community. A statement accompanying the plans says: "Mr Reilly and his family are looking for a settled environment with a permanent base to call home."
